:::{#exm-maximum-likelihood-kl-divergence}
#### The divergence from the data for coin flips

<!-- no-figure: the example is a table of divergences -->

A coin is flipped $100$ times,
and it lands heads $70$ times.
The chunk below follows @thm-maximum-likelihood-kl-divergence
for the [Bernoulli](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-bernoulli) models
with the [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) of heads $0.1, 0.2, \ldots, 0.9$.
It prints the divergence of each model from the [empirical distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/nonparametric-models.html#def-empirical-distribution),
the average [log-likelihood](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-loglik),
and minus the [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy) of the empirical distribution minus the divergence.

```{r}
#| label: maximum-likelihood-kl-divergence
n_flips <- 100
n_heads <- 70
empirical <- c(tails = n_flips - n_heads, heads = n_heads) / n_flips
success_prob <- seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.1)
empirical_entropy <- -sum(empirical * log2(empirical))
divergence <- numeric(length(success_prob))
avg_loglik <- numeric(length(success_prob))
for (j in seq_along(success_prob)) {
  model <- c(1 - success_prob[j], success_prob[j])
  divergence[j] <- sum(empirical * log2(empirical / model))
  avg_loglik[j] <- sum(empirical * log2(model))
}
decomposition <- -empirical_entropy - divergence
data.frame(
  success_prob,
  divergence = round(divergence, 4),
  avg_loglik = round(avg_loglik, 4),
  decomposition = round(decomposition, 4)
)
```

The last two columns agree,
as the proof says.
The divergence is smallest, at $`r round(min(divergence), 3)`$ [bits](entropy.qmd#def-bit),
and the average log-likelihood is largest
for the model with probability of heads $`r success_prob[which.min(divergence)]`$,
which is the fraction of heads in the data,
so that model is the empirical distribution.

:::
